intro: A busy Monday. The big themes are AI tools taking over the brand and shopping moments (Google's AI Overviews, Shopify paying shopping agents) and platforms tightening their grip on publishers and creators.

must_reads.title: Google moves AI Overviews for brand searches out of the main results
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google now shows its own AI-written description beside brand searches, where the brand's knowledge panel used to sit. When AI decides how a brand is described and which links appear, brands and creators have less control over where the click goes.

must_reads.title: Shopify 'Promoted' Preview Signals Revenue From Agentic 11/02/2026
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Shopify is testing a way to pay the developers of AI shopping agents a share of sales, which is basically affiliate commission for bots. It's an early sign that AI shopping will get its own affiliate rules, separate from the links creators share today.

must_reads.title: TikTok Shop counts brand website sales in a new 14-day LIVE metric
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: TikTok Shop will now count sales on a brand's own website (tracked by TikTok's pixel) as part of its LIVE results. Platforms are fighting to claim credit for sales that happen off their app, so measuring which link really drove a sale gets more contested.

must_reads.title: ‘They hold us hostage’: Publishers furious over terms change still can’t quit Facebook
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Publishers hate Meta's new terms letting it use their content for AI, but still can't walk away because Facebook sends them traffic. It shows the tension between platforms and the people who rely on them, which matters because Geniuslink works across all of them.

must_reads.title: Amazon, Flipkart face creator retention test as established influencers seek guaranteed fees over commissions
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Bigger creators in India are pushing Amazon and Flipkart for guaranteed fees instead of commission only. If commission-only programmes lose their best creators, retailers may have to change how they pay, which affects every affiliate link.
